description: An entity's history: its dated events (releases, launches, funding, acquisitions, partnerships) and state changes (a new CEO, a new revenue figure) in chronological order, superseded claims included, future-dated (announced) items included. Newest first when limited. Leads with headline and highlights, the main changes among the rows asked for, ranked and said as a sentence; the rows follow. Pass predicates to filter (e.g. ['released','model_release']; hf_repo_created is the day a Hugging Face repository was created, not a release date); on for one exact date, or from/to for a range; limit default 100, max 500; offset pages back (complete: false and next_offset say there is more). assertable_only keeps claims the record asserts for their own dates: a superseded CEO is assertable for the years he held the role. Each row carries its source's title: when a question names a date, answer from the rows on that date, and when several rows share a date, the title says which post each came from. Confidence ranks sources, not dates. group: true reads the entity's company group (as in entity_state): each row's entity names its record and a fact held on two records is one row (also_on). Every row carries its kind (people, money, products, models, other); kind keeps one. summary is the sentence the timeline page leads with and counts its claims by kind, over the entity's own timeline.

assertable_only.description: Only claims the record asserts for their own dates

detail.description: compact: each row is id, predicate, value, qualifier, the dates it held, status, why_not when the record does not assert it, and the primary source URL: about a fifth the size, so a page holds five times the rows. Left out: published, recorded, confidence, citation, evidence (each is on the claim page, https://asof.is/claim/{id}, or the claim tool). full (the default): every field.

entity.description: Entity slug, e.g. openai, nvidia, claude

group.description: Every record of the entity's company group, merged

offset.description: Skip this many rows, newest first (next_offset from the previous page)

on.description: Only events dated exactly this day, YYYY-MM-DD

predicates.description: Only these predicates, e.g. ['ceo'] for every CEO in turn or ['released','model_release'] for releases

view.description: news: only changes a reader would call news, that the record asserts: leadership, ownership, deals, funding, releases, board and feature changes, the main figures. Left out: Hugging Face repositories, posts, identifiers, routine balance-sheet and quarterly rows, undated claims, and unverified, flagged or retracted ones. For changes_since with an entity, news also means took effect since the date (not merely recorded since), newest first, with total. A news timeline pages by 50 unless limit says otherwise. all (the default): every row.

name: timeline

complete.description: false when rows remain: ask again with next_offset

events.description: The rows, newest first when limited

headline.description: The main changes among the rows asked for, as one sentence

legend.description: What the row fields and why_not codes mean

page.description: The page on asof.is that states the same answer

summary.description: The sentence the timeline page leads with

title: Entity timeline
